Review scope: the uncommitted working-tree changes in /Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker. Get them with `git diff HEAD` plus these three NEW untracked files which are also in scope: src/lib/utils/imageZoom.ts, src/lib/utils/imageZoom.spec.ts, src/lib/services/ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts.

Your angle is REUSE ONLY. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase already has. Grep shared/utility modules (src/lib/utils/, src/lib/tests/fixtures/, src/lib/tests/harness/) and files adjacent to the change, and name the existing helper that should be called instead.

Note this project has canonical test fixtures documented in CLAUDE.md: src/lib/tests/fixtures/supabaseMock.ts (chainable Supabase mock), rowBuilders.ts, fixtures/fetchMock.ts, and harness/appMocks.ts. Check whether the new spec files hand-roll something those already provide.

Do NOT look for correctness bugs. Do NOT report style preferences. Only concrete duplication with a named existing alternative.

Return a list of findings, each with: file, line, one-line summary, and what is duplicated. If nothing, say so plainly.

content.text:
Reviewed `git diff HEAD` plus the three new files against `src/lib/utils/`, `src/lib/tests/fixtures/`, `src/lib/tests/harness/`, and `src/lib/tests/builders/`.

First, the things I checked and cleared, so the parent agent doesn't re-litigate them:

- The `vi.mock('$lib/supabaseClient')` preamble and hand-wired storage/insert chains in `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker/src/lib/services/ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts` are **not** a duplication of `fixtures/supabaseMock.ts` — that fixture's own header explicitly excludes the `ReceiptService.*` specs ("NOT for the `ReceiptService.*` / reconciliation specs … Leave those as-is"), and `vi.mock` is hoisted per-module so the preamble cannot be import-shared.
- The new spec correctly uses `stubFetchJson` / `stubFetchReject` from `fixtures/fetchMock.ts` rather than hand-rolling a Response.
- `sourceFile()` (size-stubbed `File`) and `imageUrl()` (SVG data URL) have no existing equivalent — `rowBuilders.ts` only has `makeReceiptRow` / `makeTransactionRow` / `makeExpense` / `makeCategory`, and `Object.defineProperty(file, 'size', …)` appears nowhere else in the repo. Genuinely new.
- `appMocks.ts` is route-render scaffolding; nothing in this diff renders a route.

Findings:

findings.summary: `IMAGE_TYPES` is a verbatim copy of `RESIZABLE_TYPES` in imageResize.ts, in a file that already imports `isResizableImage` from that module.
findings.failure_scenario: The diff moved `prepareFileForUpload` (line 259) onto the shared `isResizableImage(file.type)` predicate but left `validateSourceFile` (line 192) reading the local `['image/jpeg','image/png','image/heic']` copy — `IMAGE_TYPES` now has exactly one remaining use. Adding a fourth decodable type (e.g. `image/heif`) to `RESIZABLE_TYPES` makes `resizeImage` willing to transcode it while `validateSourceFile` still rejects it with "Unsupported file type", so the new capability is unreachable and the two lists silently disagree. Line 192 should read `if (!isResizableImage(file.type) && file.type !== PDF_TYPE)` and `IMAGE_TYPES` should be deleted.

findings.summary: New `calculateFitDimensions` re-implements the aspect-preserving, never-upscale downscale already provided by `calculateResizeDimensions` in the adjacent `src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts`.
findings.failure_scenario: `calculateFitDimensions(w, h, box, box)` and `calculateResizeDimensions(w, h, box)` compute the same result (min-scale clamped at 1, aspect preserved, no enlargement) and differ only in that the resize version rounds to whole pixels and takes a square budget rather than a width/height box — i.e. the new function is a strict generalization of the existing one. The two now carry independent test suites (imageZoom.spec.ts "never enlarges an image that already fits" vs imageResize.spec.ts "should preserve dimensions if image is smaller than max size") asserting the same invariant, so a future fix to the fit rule has to be made and re-verified twice. `calculateResizeDimensions` can be expressed as a rounding wrapper over `calculateFitDimensions(w, h, maxSize, maxSize)`.
